text:
sam: :rotating_light: seeing 10x baseline requests to edge in last 3m, error rate climbing, many 503s. pattern looks like HTTP/3 bulk requests from a handful of ASNs

matt: oncall here. can you paste the alert?

sam: alert: `edge_waf_ddos_rate` triggered -> 95th p95 RPS spike. top src ASNs: AS12345, AS67890 (mobile carriers). paths: /api/v1/complete mostly POST with large cookie headers.

elena: confirming logs show HTTP/3 client hello flood + many requests with weird header permutations. looks like an amplification probe.

maya: pinging @security and @sre for mitigation. original detection doesn't show lateral authentication attempts, so far only L7 traffic.

priya: can we throttle by ASN and add a WAF ACL? prefer soft block first (challenge) not full blackhole.

matt: agreed. applying temporary rule: challenge (captcha/401) for requests from AS12345 and AS67890 at the edge. pushing now.

sre-bot: deploy:edge-waf-rule-1793456891 applied -> rule id rw-1793-block-asn-challenge (status: success)

david: seeing immediate drop in error rate from internal test clients. customer reports reduced 503s but a few mobile customers behind AS12345 still impacted. some clients fail the challenge.

elena: on the rules page I added an override to exclude certain whitelisted customer IP prefixes. snippet: ```waf.rule { match: asn in [12345,67890] action: challenge exclude_ips: [10.2.0.0/16, 52.120.0.0/20] }```

sam: FYI we have 4 customers flagged in support tickets. @account-team looped to handle comms. sending incident banner to status page now.

maya: quick security check: no key material accessed, control plane API logs look normal. I'll kick off a read-only audit of recent RBAC changes to ensure no one changed firewall keys.

priya: telemetry note: KV cache hit ratio dropped — suspect many new connection patterns bypassing caches, increasing CPU on runtime. recommend enabling prefix caching for these endpoints.

matt: created short-term autoscale for dedicated pools + bumped connection limits on edge proxies at 1793456945. should smooth out load for legitimate customers.

david: also added a rate-limit rule: `global:200/min per-ip` for the paths under /api/v1/complete to limit abuse without breaking UX for normal mobile.

elena: logs show some requests coming from spoofed UA strings and rotating cookies -> classic bot farm. blocking UA patterns too.

maya: confirm: no indicator of data exfiltration. this is volumetric L7 abuse. marking Sev2 for now.

sam: status page update posted: 'We are mitigating elevated traffic from a subset of mobile carriers, some customers may see transient errors. Engineers working on targeted mitigations.'

priya: next actions I propose: (1) schedule postmortem, (2) add ASN-based alerting and automated challenge rule, (3) update runbook with HTTP/3-specific checks, (4) create a short lived RBAC role for emergency WAF edits with audit logging turned on.

maya: adding to security tasks: ensure WAF change events are forwarded to SIEM (log-ship) and ensure KMS usage for rule signing is present. I'll request a KMS key rotation for the rule-signing key as a precaution and log that in the incident timeline.

matt: good. I'll open a ticket for postmortem and assign owners. quick note: we should not escalate to blackhole unless sustained for >30m or collateral damage high.

david: support update: account-team emailed affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA. no SLA credits recommended yet.

sam: monitoring: p95 latency and 5xxs down to normal after challenge + rate-limit changes. keeping this thread open for 1h to watch for secondary spikes.

elena: after-action item: add an automated play: when edge RPS > x and top ASNs count > 3 -> auto-challenge + notify security + create incident.

maya: will run RBAC audit and post results in #sec-audit tomorrow. also confirming KMS rotation scheduled in 48h.

matt: thanks all. marking incident as mitigated for now, will update thread with postmortem link once done. :thumbsup:
